title: Severe bleeding

source.name: Stop the Bleed — U.S. Department of Homeland Security

steps: Make sure the scene is safe for you.
Call or radio for help now.
Find where the bleeding is coming from. Expose the wound.
Press hard and directly on the wound with a clean cloth or gauze.
If an arm or leg keeps bleeding through pressure, apply a tourniquet two to three inches above the wound, not on a joint.
Tighten the tourniquet until the bleeding stops. Note the time it was applied.
For a deep wound that cannot take a tourniquet, pack it tightly with gauze, then keep pressing.
Keep pressure on until help takes over.
callForHelp: Bleeding that will not stop with firm pressure
